questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Thalamus is
questions.solution: The broadened base of flower which lies at the tip of pedicel is called torus or thalamus or receptacle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pentamerous actinomorphic flowers, bicarpellary ovary with oblique septa, and fruit capsule or berry are characteristic features of family
questions.solution: A pentamerous actinomorphic flower is one where the floral parts are in multiples of five and the flower can be divided into two equal halves in more than one plane. The gynoecium is bicarpellary, syncarpous, forming a superior bilocular ovary. Each locule has many ovules on axile placentation. Members of Solanaceae are characterized by the presence of an obliquely placed septum in the ovary and highly swollen placentae. The oblique septum is probably due to shifting in the position of the ovary.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correctly matched pair among the following.
questions.solution: Pea plant belongs to the Fabaceae family characterized by a zygomorphic, bisexual flower with five sepals (gamosepalous), imbricate aestivation, five petals (polypetalous), papilionaceous, consisting of a posterior standard, two lateral wings, two anterior ones forming a keel (enclosing stamens and pistil), vexillary aestivation. The androecium is ten, diadelphous, with dithecous anther. Gynoecium with the superior ovary, monocarpellary, unilocular with many ovules, and a single style. Leguminous fruit: legume with one too many non-endospermic seeds.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tobacco and Petunia belong to the family
questions.solution: Tobacco plant (Nicotiana tabacum) yields tobacco, while Petunia is an ornamental plant. Both the plants are the member of family Solanaceae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In some plants, the leaves are short-lived and small. The petioles of such plants expand and become green. One such plant is:
questions.solution: In some plants such as Australian acacia, the leaves are small and short-lived. The petioles in these plants expand, become green and synthesise food.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Arrangement of sepals and petals with respect to each other in the floral bud is called
questions.solution: Number of sepals and petals are more in a flower thus they show a specific pattern of arrangement called aestivation which is clearly visible in bud condition.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Root caps are absent in
questions.solution: The root cap's primary function is enhancing direct root growth by reducing friction against the soil, sensing gravity and protecting root meristem. In hydrophytes, the root system will be of a fibrous type and hence, the root pockets are present, whereas the root caps are absent, e.g., Eichhornia, Pistia, Lemna. Pandanus, Pothos and Ficus are plants that grow on soil.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The edible part of coconut fruit is:
questions.solution: The cellular and nuclear endosperm is the edible part of the drupe fruit of coconut.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Epipetalous and epiphyllous condition are respectively seen in:
questions.solution: The androecium consists of stamens. These stamens can be attached to the petal, this condition is known as an epipetalous condition. Such a condition is seen in Brinjal. Epiphyllous when stamens are attached to the perianth as in the flowers of lily.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The expression 'gynoecium is polycarpellary apocarpous' implies that the
options: Gynoecium comprises only one pistil which is fused with the stamen
Gynoecium comprises more than one carpel, all of which are free
Gynoecium comprises only one carpel which is free
Gynoecium comprises more than one carpel which are fused
questions.solution: Gynoecium having a single carpel is called monocarpellary (two carpels: bicarpellary, three: tricarpellary, many: polycarpellary). Carpels may be free, then the gynoecium is called apocarpous (e.g., polycarpellary apocarpous in rose, lotus and Ranunculus) and when they are fused, the gynoecium is known to be syncarpous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The technical term used for the androecium in a flower of china rose (Hibiscus rosa Sinensis) is
questions.solution: China rose of Malvaceae family possess numerous stamens. The filaments of stamens are united in one group thus forming a staminal tube around the style. Such stamens are called monadelphous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following are the members of the family Fabaceae?

Gram, belladonna, arhar, moong, potato, Indigofera, pea, tobacco, Sesbania
questions.solution: Fabaceae is a family of dicot plants, mostly legumes. The members of these families have a distinct floral characteristic which shows vexillary aestivation in the petal arrangement. Some important members of this family are pea, Soyabean, Sesbania, lupin, gram, arhar, moong, Indigofera. The other examples like belladonna, potato, and tobacco belong to the family Solanaceae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another without any particular direction, the condition is termed as:
questions.solution: When the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another without any particular direction, the condition is termed as imbricate aestivation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The aestivation that may be seen in the sepals of family Papilionoideae is
questions.solution: Family Papilionoideae also called Fabaceae, has 5 sepals in the calyx. Many members show fused on gamosepalous while others may show valvate or imbricate aestivation. They have 5 petals that show vexillary aestivation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The condition with the united calyx in a flower is called as
questions.solution: The calyx is the outermost whorl of the flower. It is made of units called sepals. These sepals can be united/fused or can be free from each other. The gamosepalous condition shows that the sepals are united. The polysepalous condition shows that the sepals are free from each other.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In guava plant
options: leaves show opposite phyllotaxy while flowers are epigynous
leaves show opposite phyllotaxy while flowers are hypogynous
leaves show alternate phyllotaxy while flowers are epigynous
leaves show alternate phyllotaxy while flowers are hypogynous
questions.solution: In guava, there are two leaves present at a node. Thus, it shows the opposite phyllotaxy. In guava, all the whorls of a flower are attached above the gynoecium. Thus, it has epigynous flowers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Identify the correct match between the types of stem modifications and their examples.
 
Column I Column II
i. Stem tendril a. Citrus
ii. Fleshy photosynthetic stem b. Strawberry
iii. Woody thorns c. Watermelon
iv. Underground horizontal stem d. Opuntia
questions.solution: Stem tendril is a structural modification of stem for mechanical support, e.g., strawberry, cucumber. Fleshy stem known as the phylloclade is a modification of plants like Opuntia in dessert regions in order to conserve water and perform photosynthesis. Woody thorns are seen in plants like citrus for protection for herbivores. Horizontal stems are seen in plants like strawberry which help them propagate vegetatively.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements about a leaf. Which amongst them are correct?

I. The swollen leaf-base mainly seen in leguminous plants is called the pulvinus.
II. The axillary bud arises from the axil formed by the leaf.
III. The leaf lamina is generally flat but may vary in shape and size from plant to plant.
questions.solution: The leaf is the main photosynthetic organ of the plant. It majorly consists of the leaf base, petiole, and the leaf lamina. Sometimes the swollen leaf base, called pulvinus, is seen in leguminous plants. The leaf generally emerges from the node of the stem where it forms an axil through which an axillary bud emerges. This axillary bud further develops into a branch. The leaf lamina serves as the stage for harvesting light for photosynthesis. The shape of the leaf may vary from plant to plant

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct difference between the ovary of rose and china rose is
options: Rose has superior ovary while China rose has inferior ovary
Rose has inferior ovary while China rose has superior ovary
Rose has semi-inferior ovary while China rose has inferior ovary
Rose has semi-inferior ovary while China rose has superior ovary
questions.solution: Rose has perigynous flowers in which the gynoecium is present in the center and other whorls of the flower are located on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level. Thus, it has a semi-inferior ovary. China rose has hypogynous flowers in which all the floral whorls are attached below the gynoecium. Thus, it has superior ovary.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What kind of modification for propagation is seen in ginger and banana?
options: Modification of tap root for food storage
Modification of adventitious root for food storage
Modification of stem for food storage
Zaminkand as modification of root and turmericas modified stem
questions.solution: Rhizome is horizontal underground plant stem capable of producing the shoot and root systems of a new plant. Rhizomes are used to store starches and proteins (ginger, banana, turmeric, etc).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Zygomorphic flower and diadelphous condition are found in the family
questions.solution: Members of Fabaceae family has zygomorphic flower which can be divided into  <math><mn>2</mn></math>  equal halves from only one vertical plane. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: Perigynous flower is found in Rose.
The keel is the characteristic feature of tulips.
The gynoecium consists of many free pistils in Michelia.
The perianth is present in the flowers of Lily.
questions.solution: Members of the Rosaceae family, like rose, peach, apple show perigynous condition. Keels are the smallest petals of Papillonaceous corolla having vexillary aestivation which is a characteristic feature of the Fabaceae family. Tulip is a member of the Liliaceae family.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Fruit of mango is ___(P)___, developing from ___(Q)____, ____(R)_____ ovaries and are ____(S)____.
options:

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find out a set of common N<sub>2</sub> fixing fodder plants.
questions.solution: Sesbania and Trifolium are fodder of Fabaceae famaily. They have root nodules in which Rhizobium lives symbiotically carrying out nitrogen fixation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The modified stem of Opuntia is
questions.solution: In Opuntia, the stem becomes green and photosynthetic and performs the function of a leaf. Leaves are reduced to spines to reduce transpiration. Phyllode is petiole modification in which petiole becomes flat leaf-like and carries out photosynthesis.

questions.solution: The position of the ovary in a flower can be different for different flowers. Some flowers have a superior ovary (hypogyny), where all the other parts of the flower are below it. Some flowers have a half-inferior ovary (perigyny), gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level. Such condition is seen in peach.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following family can be associated with the characteristics given below?

(i) Racemose inflorescence.
(ii) Vexillary aestivation in corolla.
(iii) Bracteate, complete, bisexual, zygomorphic flower.
questions.solution: The flowers of family Fabaceae show vexillary aestivation, which explains the Papilionaceous (butterfly-shaped) flower. It also shows the presence of diadelphous condition where the stamens are arranged in a (9) + 1 arrangement, meaning out of the 10 stamens, 9 are united in a bundle and one is free. Pisum sativum is an excellent example of this family showing both these characteristics precisely.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following would you find retained endospermic tissue even after the formation of the seed?
questions.solution: In some seeds, the endosperm is retained in the form of a food storing tissue. These seeds are called endospermic seeds which are found in rice, barley, coffee, and castor. The seeds in which the endosperm is completely consumed by the developing embryo. Such seeds are called non-endospermic seeds which include sunflower, bean, and gram.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following floral formula represents the mustard plant?
questions.solution:
Flower formula of mustard plant is



Cruciferae (Mustard family) diagnostic characters:
1. Habit: Annual, biennial or perennial herbs.

2. Roots: Tap root (fibrous or tuberous)

3. Stem: Herbaceous.

4. Leaves: Petiolate, alternate, simple, exstipulate, reticulate venation; leaves are generally covered by simple or branched hairs.

5. Inflorescence: Simple racemose. It becomes corymbose raceme.

6. Flower: Pedicillate, ebracteate. actinomorphic, regular.

7. Complete, hermaphrodite, hypogynous.

8. Calyx: 4 sepals, free, dimerous (placed in two whorls) green

9. Corolla: 4 petals, free arranged in single whorl occupying the diagonal position and form characteristics cruciform form.

10. Stamens: 6 stamens, free, tetradynamous (two lateral stamens are smaller but four median stamens are larger) basifixed; nectaries are present at the base of stamens.

11. Carpel: 2 carpels, fused to form compound ovary: syncarpous. placentation parietal, ovary unilocular but become hilocular due to formation of false septum.
12. Fruits: Siliqua or silicula.
13. Seed: Non-endosperm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Perigynous flower and diadelphous condition are found in the family
questions.solution: The tendency of cohesion of stamen results in diadelphous condition. In perigynous flowers, a hypanthium (a floral tube formed from the fusion of the stamens, petals, and sepals) is attached to the receptacle below the gynoecium and surrounds the ovary; the ovary is superior, and the free parts of the petals, sepals, and stamens are attached to the rim of the hypanthium. Perigynous flower and diadelphous condition are found in the family Papilionaceae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: 'The placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and the ovules are borne on this ridge forming two rows'. This statement explains
questions.solution:
The arrangement of ovules within the ovary is known as placentation. The placentation is of different types namely, marginal, axile, parietal, basal, central, and free central. In marginal placentation, the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and the ovules are borne on this ridge forming two rows.
Example: pea family.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following figures represents the placentation in Primrose?
questions.solution: The figure given in option (b) represents the placetation (free central). In free central placentation, ovary is unilocular and ovules are borne on the axis in the center of the ovary and septa are absent. It is also seen Dianthus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Composite fruit is developed from:
questions.solution: When a fruit develops from entire inflorescence it is called composite or multiple fruit. Syconous and sorosis are two important composite fruit.

questions.solution: Underground stem of plants like potato, ginger, turmeric, zamikand and Colocasia stores food and helps the plant to survive during unfavourable condition.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Parietal placentation is observed in:
questions.solution: In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on the peripheral part. The ovary is one-chambered but it becomes two-chambered due to the formation of the false septum, e.g., mustard and Argemone.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following properties are seen in the brinjal plant?

Legume fruit, alternate phyllotaxy, actinomorphic flower, hypogynous flower, bicarpellary-syncarpous gynoecium, non-endospermic seeds
questions.solution:
Brinjal belongs to the family Solanaceae. The characteristics of Solanaceae are:

Habit: Mostly herbs and shrubs. Underground stem tubers are found in potato.
Leaves: In vegetative parts, alternate and floral regions, opposite
always exstipulate, simple, rarely pinnately compound as in potato and tomato.
Inflorescence: Cymose or solitary
Flower: Ebracteate, Pedicellate, complete, actinomorphic, bisexual.
Calyx: Consists of five sepals, gamosepalous, valvate. Sepals are usually persistent (e.g. brinjal, chilly, tomato, etc).
Corolla: Consists of five petals, gamopetalous, evaluate or twisted.
Androecium: Consists of five stamens, epipetalous altering with corolla lobes. Anther dithecous.
Gynoecium: Bicarpellary, syncarpous, bilocular, ovary superior and ovules are numerous on axial placentation.
Fruit: Berry or capsule.
Seeds: Many, endospermic .
Economic Importance: Many plants belonging to this family are a source of food (tomato, brinjal, potato), spice (chilli), medicine (belladonna, ashwagandha), fumigatory (tobacco), ornamentals (petunia).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A plant with racemose inflorescence, zygomorphic flowers, five sepals and petals showing vexillary aestivation, monocarpellary and unilocular superior ovary, androecium consisting of ten stamens.

The above-listed conditions are characteristics of which family of plants?
questions.solution: The given characteristics belong to the members of the family Fabaceae. These are plants with racemose inflorescence, zygomorphic flowers, five sepals and petals showing vexillary aestivation, monocarpellary and unilocular superior ovary, androecium consisting of ten stamens. The above floral formula stands corrected for plants like soybean, grams, pulses and Sesbania.

In lemon, there are many stamens whose filaments are fused together to form more than two bundles. Lemons have axile placentation in which the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In Australian acacia, the petioles expand, become green and synthesize food.
If more than two leaves arise at a node and form a whorl, it is called whorled, as in mustard.
In palmately compound leaves, the leaflets are attached at a common point, i.e., at the tip of the petiole, as in silk cotton.
Leaves of dicotyledonous plants generally possess reticulate venation, while parallel venation is the characteristic of most monocotyledons.

Types of Aestivation Examples

ii. Twisted b. Bean
iii. Imbricate c. Calotropis

questions.solution: Calotropis is an example of valvate aestivation in which the petals touch each other without overlapping. Cotton flower shows twisted aestivation in which the one margin of a petal overlaps the next petal. Imbricate aestivation shows the petals overlapping each other without any specific direction, such as that in Gulmohar. Bean belongs to the Fabaceae family in which the flowers have a unique five-petal arrangement called the vexillary arrangement.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the given diagrams, A (spine) and B (tendril) are structures which are modifications of the stem. Then, probable examples of plants in which A and B can be observed, respectively, will be:
questions.solution:
Modifications of stem:

1. Underground stems may modify to store food.

Examples - potato, turmeric, ginger, Colocasia, zaminkand, etc.

2. Stem may develop into tendrils (originating from axillary buds) for support.

Examples - grapevines and gourds (cucumber, pumpkins and watermelons).

3. Stems may develop woody and pointed thorns for protection from the axillary buds.

Examples - Bougainvillea, Citrus.

4. Stems may develop chlorophyll and perform photosynthesis.

Examples - Opuntia (stem as flattened structures), Euphorbia (stem as fleshy cylindrical structures), etc.

5. Stems may help in spread and vegetative propagation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following properties. Which of these are seen in mango as well as coconut?

I. The fruit is called a drupe.
II. The fruit is developed from superior ovaries.
III. The fruit is one-seeded.
IV. The middle layer of the fruit wall is edible.
questions.solution: In mango and coconut, the fruit is known as a drupe. They develop from monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one-seeded. In mango, the pericarp is well-differentiated into an outer thin epicarp, a middle fleshy edible mesocarp and an inner stony hard endocarp. In coconut, which is also a drupe, the mesocarp is fibrous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The term phyllotaxy is used to describe
options: type of ovary in a plant
mode of arrangement of leaves on the stem
arrangement of sepals and petals in a flower.
questions.solution: The arrangement of leaves on the stem and its branches is called phyllotaxy. The significance of this arrangement is to help leaves getting maximum sunlight for photosynthesis.

Tomato, brinjal and potato belong to family Solanaceae. Gloriosa, Aloe and Asparagus belong to family Liliaceae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Observe the following flowers and state the correct explanation about them:
options: A is a hypogynous flower while B is a perigynous flower
A is a perigynous flower while B is a hypogynous flower
Both A and B are hypogynous flowers
Both A and B are perigynous flowers
questions.solution: In the hypogynous flower, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior, e.g., mustard, china rose and brinjal. If gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level, it is called perigynous. The ovary here is said to be half inferior, e.g., plum rose, peach. In both the flowers depicted in the diagram, the floral whorls are inserted on the rim of the thalamus. Hence, they are perigynous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In china rose, the flowers are
questions.solution: China rose (Hibiscus), the flower is actinomorphic; thus, it can be divided into two equal halves from any vertical plane passing through the centre. Ovary is superior (hypogynous) and petals shows twisted aestivation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these statements regarding modified roots and stem is incorrect?
options: In Asparagus, adventitious root is modified for food storage
Prop roots are for mechanical support
Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand and colocasia are modified for photosynthesis
Onion is an example of modified shoot
questions.solution: Asparagus has fasciculated roots that arise in a bunch from a lower node of the stem and become fleshy for the storage of food. It is a type of modified adventitious root. Underground stems of potato (tuber), ginger and turmeric (rhizome), zaminkand and colocasia (corm) are used for food storage and vegetative propagation. Onion is a modified underground stem called the bulb. This stem is reduced and has a disc-like structure and surrounds with numerous fleshly scaly leaves.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The mismatched pair among the following is:
options: Variation in the length of stamen filaments - Salvia
questions.solution: Adelphy is a condition in which the stamens are joined together only by their filaments while anthers are free. If there is only one bundle of stamens it is called monadelphy. This is commonly seen in Hibiscus. If there are two bundles of stamens it is called diadelphy. This is commonly seen in gram and pea. If there are more than two bundles of stamens it is called polyadelphy. This is commonly seen in Citrus and castor. In Cucurbita, anthers as well as filaments of stamens are united through their whole length. This is called synandry. Salvia has lever mechanism with variable length of filaments which helps in pollination by insects.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
What is the correct difference between the following diagrams?



              (I)                                              (II)
options: Absence of sub-stomatal chamber in both types of the leaves in (I).
questions.solution: I is the cross section of dicot leaf while II is the cross section of monocot leaf. In dicot leaf, the mesophyll cells are differentiated into palisade cells which are closely placed and spongy cells which are loosely placed. In dicot leaf, stomata are present on the lower surface. Thus sub-stomatal chambers are present only on the lower surface. In monocot leaf, stomata are present on the upper as well as the lower surface. Thus sub-stomatal chambers are present only on both the surfaces.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Identify the correct statements about the angiospermic embryo.

i. The scutellum is centrally placed in monocots.
ii. Plumule is the stem tip and radicle is the root tip in dicots.
iii. Coleorrhiza is part of the hypocotyl in monocots.
iv. Monocotyledonous zygote gives rise to a globular heart-shaped embryo.
questions.solution: Scutellum/cotyledon is situated laterally in monocots. Cotyledons are centrally placed in dicots. Plumule is the stem tip and radicle is the root tip in dicots. Coleoptile and coleorhiza is the stem tip and root tip in monocots respectively. Dicotyledonous zygote gives rise to a globular heart shaped embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Flower is perigynous and the ovary is said to be half-inferior in
questions.solution: A half-inferior ovary (also known as half-superior, sub-inferior or partially inferior) is embedded or surrounded by the receptacle. Such flowers are termed perigynous or half-epigynous. The flower is perigynous, and the ovary is said to be half-inferior in rose, peach and plum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following columns.
 
Column-I Column- II
 (A) Underground stem  (1) Euphorbia
 (B) Stem tendril  (2) Opuntia
 (C) Stem thorns  (3) Potato
 (D) Flattened stem  (4) Citrus
 (E) Fleshy cylindrical stem  (5) Cucumber
questions.solution:
Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zamikand, Colocasia, are modified to store food in them.
In Cucmber, extra-axillary bud develops into stem tendril.
Axillary buds of stems of some plants like Citrus, Bougainvillea get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns to protect them from browsing animals.
Some plants of arid regions modify their stems into flattened (e.g., Opuntia) of fleshy cylindrical (e.g., Euphorbia) structures. They contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following types of roots are correctly matched with their examples?

I. Apogeotropic roots: Rhizophora
II. Absence of calyptra: Lemna
III. Velamen containing roots: Vanda
IV. Moniliform roots: Portulaca
questions.solution: Apogeotropic means negatively geotropic roots. They are seen in halophytes that grow in oxygen-deficient soil. So the root grows vertically upwards. They are also called pneumatophores. They are seen in Rhizophora, Sonneratia, Heritiera, etc. The Calyptra is a root cap. It is absent in hydrophytes that float on water such as Lemna, Pistia, etc. Velamen is hygroscopic roots found in epiphytes (plants which grow on large trees) such as Vanda. Moniliform roots are beaded roots found in Mimordica, Portulaca, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Corm is a modification of
questions.solution: A stem is modified into various forms to perform a variety of functions like storage, vegetative propagation, etc. A corm is a type of underground modified stem which is spherical, branched, vertically growing with a diameter more than length. It bears reduced nodes and internodes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following (with respect to flowers and family).

(1) Actinomorphic, trimerous (a) Solanaceae
(2) Zygomorphic, pentamerous (b) Liliaceae
(3) Actinomorphic, pentamerous (c) Cruciferae
(4) Actinomorphic, tetramerous ( d ) Fabaceae
questions.solution: Actinomorphic and trimerous flowers are found in the Liliaceae family. Actinomorphic and tetramerous flowers are found in the Brassicaceae family. Zygomorphic and pentamerous flowers are seen in the Fabaceae family.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following is not a character of racemose?

a. The floral axis shows continuous growth
b. The basal flower is older, and the apical flower is younger.
c. The flower opens from the periphery to the centre.
d. The arrangement is basipetal.
questions.solution: The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis is termed an inflorescence. Depending on whether the apex gets developed into a flower or continues to grow, two major types of inflorescences are defined: racemose and cymose. In the racemose type of inflorescences, the main axis continues to grow, the flowers are borne laterally in an acropetal succession.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a medicinal plant?
questions.solution: Muliathi (Glycirrhizae), a member of Fabaceae, Aloe vera, a member of Liliaceae family, and Belladonna (Atropa belladonna), a member of Solanaceae family, are all medicinal plants. Indigofera commonly called the Nile is used to obtain dye.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

ii. The arrangement of the ovule in the ovary is called ___B___.

options:

questions.solution: The arrangement of the ovule in the ovary is called placentation. In tap roots, younger roots are at apex and mature roots are at the base. The inflorescence is the arrangement of the flowers on a common axis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In monocotyledon seed, the outermost layer of endosperm is called
questions.solution: The outermost layer of the endosperm of monocots is called the Aleurone layer, it consists of enzymatic proteins which help in breakdown of stored food and supply it to the embryo during the germination of seed. Ploidy of cells of the aleurone layer is <math><mtext>3n</mtext></math>.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tetradynamous conditions are present in the plants of which Family?
questions.solution: Tetradynamous means six stamens (2+4), in which filaments of two outer stamens are smaller, while four inner stamen filaments are longer. This condition is commonly seen in Brassica or the crucifer family.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following columns.

II Perianth (b) b) Lily- Liliaceae

IV Persistent sepals (d) d) Mustard - Brassicaceae
questions.solution:
In vexillary aestivation, the five petals are arranged in a descending imbricate manner and are observed in Fabaceae.

Perianth is also called tepal. The fused sepals and petals are called as perianth and are observed in Liliaceae.

False septum, also called replum which divides the unilocular ovary into bilocular and bilocular ovary into tetralocular ovary, is observed in mustard plant.

Persistent sepals are observed in the Solanaceae family.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Modification in the form of leaf spines and stem thorns is observed in
questions.solution: Leaf spines are the modification of leaves. They reduce the loss of water and protect the plant. Stem thorns are the modification of stems. They are woody, strong and help in protection and climbing for woody climber plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Calotropis, the leaves show (X) phyllotaxy while the petals show (Y) aestivation.
questions.solution:
When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, it is said to be valvate.

If one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one and so on, it is called twisted. Calotropis has valvate aestivation. In alternate type of phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner. In opposite type, a pair of leaves arise at each node and lie opposite to each other as in Calotropis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following fruit develops from monocarpellary or multicarpellary, syncarpous ovary and forms a single fruit?
questions.solution: When a single fruit develops from a single flower having one or many syncarpous ovaries, it is called a simple fruit. It can be dry or fleshy depending on the nature of the fruit wall called the pericarp.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Examine the diagram given below and identify the angiosperm family to which it belongs to.
questions.solution: Solanaceae is commonly called as the 'potato family'. They have 5 petals and 5 sepals and hence they have pentamerous symmetry. They have two carpels in their gynoecium which are fused together (syncarpous condition). They have a bilocular superior ovary with axile placentation (placenta swollen).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of stem and leaf tendril, respectively?
questions.solution: Stem tendrils that develop from axillary buds are slender and spirally coiled and help plants to climb, e.g., in gourds (cucumber, pumpkins, watermelon) and grapevines. Leaves are converted into tendrils for climbing, as in peas, or into spines for defence, as in cacti.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The proteinaceous endosperm of maize is called
questions.solution: In maize, endosperm, the outermost layer of endosperm cells, becomes specialized and becomes rich in proteins. These enzymatic proteins cause breakdown of stored food in endosperm during germination and transfer it to the embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following plants has a zygomorphic flower?
questions.solution: Flower is said to show three types of symmetry. They are actinomorphic, zygomorphic and asymmetric. Asymmetric the word itself says that the flower cannot be divided in equal parts by any method. In actinomorphic, the flower can be divided into two equal halves radially and when it can be divided into equal halves only through one vertical plane is known as zygomorphic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

B. Pistia and Eichhornia are examples of offset.

questions.solution: In Euphorbia, the stem becomes fleshy green and cylindrical and carries out photosynthesis. Such stem is called phylloclade. Pistia and Eichhornia are aquatic plants, in which stem is one and two-internode long and bears tuff of roots and bunches of leaves at nodes.

questions.subject: Botany

It has an actinomorphic flower and imbricate aestivation of petals
It has a zygomorphic flower and twisted aestivation of petals
It has an actinomorphic flower and twisted aestivation of petals
questions.solution: The flower of Cassia can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane. Hence, it is a zygomorphic flower. The margins of petals of Cassia overlap one another but not in any particular direction. Hence, it shows imbricate aestivation.

questions.solution: Aestivation is the arrangement of the flower petals. In calotropis, valvate aestivation is observed. Phyllotaxy is the arrangement pattern on leaves. In Silk cotton, the palmately compound leaf is seen. In Lilly flower, the stamens are free and versatile and non-epipetalous in nature.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Indigofera (dye), Sesbania (fodder), groundnut (oil yielding plant), and gram (pulse) all are members of the Fabaceae family which shows zygomorphic flowers due to vexillary aestivation.

Corolla: petals five, gamopetallous with valvate aestivation
Gynoecium: bicarpellary, syncarpous with bilocular, superior ovary superior
Seeds: many seeds in a fruit, without endosperm

questions.solution: Parthenocarpic fruits are developed without any fertilization of the ovary. These fruits are seedless. Seedless banana is an example. In monocot seeds, the large shield shape cotyledon is known as scutellum. The endosperm is covered by a proteinous layer called aleurone layer that separates the endosperm from the embryo and nourishes it. The attachment of seeds to fruit leaves a scar on a seed coat called hilum.

The general characters of Liliaceae family is the flowers are bracteate, bisexual, complete, actinomorphic symmetry, hypogynous and trimerous, epiphyllous and in some plants may be epipetalous. They have polyandrous andoecium and superior ovary.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Observe the following leaf of papaya and state its type.
questions.solution: A leaf is said to be simple, when its lamina is entire or when incised, the incisions do not touch the midrib. In this leaf, the incisions don't reach the midrib so it is a simple palmate leaf. When the incisions of the lamina reach up to the midrib breaking it into a number of leaflets, the leaf is called compound. The compound leaves may be of two types: In a pinnately compound leaf, a number of leaflets are present on a common axis, the rachis, which represents the midrib of the leaf as in neem. In palmately compound leaves, the leaflets are attached at a common point, i.e., at the tip of the petiole, as in silk cotton. A leaf having divisions that are themselves compound are called decompound leaves.

During unfavourable conditions, the aerial part of the plant dies but the stem bulbs survive and develop into shoots.
Its flower has three green sepals and three pink petals
It is placed in the same family as that of Colchicum autumnale
questions.solution: Allium cepa is onion. It shows cymose inflorescence with umbellate clusters. It consists of a number of short flower stalks which spread from a common point like umbrella. The position of the mother axis with respect to the flower
questions.solution: A floral diagram provides information about the number of parts of a flower, their arrangement, and the relation they have with one another. The position of the mother axis with respect to the flower is represented by a dot on the top of the floral diagram. Calyx, corolla, androecium, and gynoecium are drawn in successive whorls, calyx being the outermost and the gynoecium being in the center. The floral formula also shows cohesion and adhesion within parts of whorls and between whorls.

questions.q: Mustard contains

Flowers are termed syncarpous when carpels are fused, as in mustard and tomato. In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part. questions.solution:
The mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in the floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl is known as aestivation. The main types of aestivation are valvate, twisted, imbricate, and vexillary.

In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous (Figure A). When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, as in Calotropis, it is said to be valvate (Figure B). If the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction as in Cassia and Gulmohar, the aestivation is called imbricate (Figure C). If one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one and so on as in china rose, lady's finger and cotton, it is called twisted (Figure D).

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution:
The arrangement of ovules within the ovary is known as placentation. The placentation are of different types namely, marginal, axile, parietal, basal, central and free central.

When the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary, the placentaion is said to be axile (Figure A), as in china rose, tomato and lemon.

When the ovules are borne on central axis and septa are absent, as in Dianthus (carnation) and Primrose the placentation is called free central. (Figure B)

In marginal placentation (Figure C) the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and the ovules are borne on this ridge forming two rows, as in pea.

In parietal placentation (Figure D), the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part. Ovary is one-chambered but it becomes two chambered due to the formation of the false septum, e.g., mustard and Argemone.

options: Possess different floral appendages at successive nodes

questions.solution:
Flower is defined as modified dwarf shoot which is meant for sexual reproduction. It is characteristic feature of angiosperm.

The flowers are termed pedicellate if they possess stalks and sessile if they lack them. The flower may be described as complete if it bears all the floral parts and incomplete, when one or more floral parts are absent. Flowers are called bisexual if they bear both androecium and gynoecium. The unisexual flowers have either androecium or gynoecium. The unisexual flowers may be male flowers or female flowers. The male flower are also called staminate flowers as they have stamens only.

The female flowers have only the carpels and hence called pistillate flowers. Flowers with sterile sex organs are described as neutral flowers. According to the distribution of male, female and bisexual flowers, various patterns are recognized.

questions.solution: The female reproductive part of the flower known as gynoecium consists of stigma, style and ovary. After fertilization ovary develops into a fruit. Q In all leguminous plants, the leaf base may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus

R The lamina or leaf blade is the green expanded part of the leaf with vein and veinlets

S Veins provide rigidity to leaf blade
questions.solution: The leaf is divided into three parts - leaf base, petiole and lamina or leaf blade. Leaf base is a junction between the leaf and stem and in monocotyledons, it forms a sheath covering the stem completely or partially. In some leguminous plants, it swells up which is called a pulvinus. Petiole helps to hold the leaf blade allowing it to flutter in wind. The leaf blade is extended green part consisting of veins and veinlets which provide rigidity as well as transport food, water and minerals. In monocots, leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly.

questions.solution: When a flower can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic, e.g., pea, gulmohur, bean, Cassia. The flower of the angiosperm plant can be categorized depending on the arrangement of the whorls around the gynoecium.

Epigynous flowers have the ovary is in the inferior position as the thalamus surrounds the ovary and may even fuse with it. The other whorls develop over the thalamus. This arrangement is shown by guava, cucumber and ray florets of sunflower.

If the ovary position is above the thalamus, that is superior to other whorls, the arrangement is called hypogynous. Mustard, brinjal develop such flowers.

When the gynoecium and other whorls are arranged almost at same level, the flower is called perigynous and ovary position is considered half inferior. Plum plant has such type of flower arrangement.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The ovary is said to be hypogynous in the flowers of
questions.solution:
The flower of the angiosperm plant can be categorized depending on the arrangement of the whorls around the gynoecium.

Epigynous flowers have the ovary is in the inferior position as the thalamus surrounds the ovary and may even fuse with it. The other whorls develop over the thalamus. This arrangement is shown by guava, cucumber and ray florets of sunflower.

If the ovary position is above the thalamus, that is superior to other whorls, the arrangement is called hypogynous. Mustard, brinjal develop such flowers.

When the gynoecium and other whorls are arranged almost at same level, the flower is called perigynous and ovary position is considered half inferior. Peach plant has such type of flower arrangement.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The following diagrams represent the types of aestivation in corolla. Identify the correct combination of labelling.
questions.solution:
The mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl is known as aestivation. The main types of aestivation are valvate, twisted, imbricate and vexillary.
In valvate, sepals or petals just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, e.g., Calotropis.
In twisted, one margin of sepal or petal overlaps that of the next one and so on, e.g., China rose, lady’s finger, cotton, etc.
In imbricate, The margins of sepal or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction e.g., Cassia, Goldmohur.
In vexillary, the largest posterior petal (vexillum or standard) overlaps two lateral petals (alae or wings) which in turn overlaps the two smallest, anterior but united petals (keel or carina), e.g., pea, bean etc.

Read the following matches regarding the placentation

(i) Primrose - Free central

(ii) Pea - Marginal

(iii) Marigold - Basal

(iv) Poppy - Axile

Which of these are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Placentation is the arrangement of the ovules in the ovary and their attachment to it. Placentation are of various type in the angiosperms - marginal, axile, central, parietal, basal, and free central. In marginal placentation, ovules are attached to the ridge formed on the ventral suture of the ovary. The Pea plant has this arrangement.

In parietal, the ovules are attached to the inner wall or towards the periphery of the ovary, observed in mustard plant and even argemone and poppy. Sunflower and marigold show basal placentation where the ovules are attached at the base of the ovary. Dianthus and primrose display free-central placentation and in it the ovules are attached at the central axis of the ovary without any septa present like in axile pattern.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In monocotyledons, the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly.
In some grasses, the leaf base may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus.
The leaf blade is the green expanded part of the leaf with veins and veinlets.
Leaves originate from shoot apical meristems and are arranged in an acropetal order.
questions.solution:
The leaf is a lateral, generally flattened structure borne on the stem. It develops at the node and bears a bud in its axil. The axillary bud later develops into a branch. Leaves originate from shoot apical meristems and are arranged in an acropetal order.

In monocotyledons, the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly. In some leguminous plants, the leaf base may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus. The lamina or the leaf blade is the green expanded part of the leaf with veins and veinlets. There is, usually, a middle prominent vein, which is known as the midrib. Veins provide rigidity to the leaf blade and act as channels of transport for water, minerals and food materials.

Fabaceae, a.k.a. Leguminosae is the family of plant having legumes, peas group in them. This group is the third largest group and economically important family of flowering plants. Solanaceae also called 'potato family' are found in regions of tropics, subtropics and temperate zones. Mostly have herbs and shrubs types of plants. The male reproductive part in the floral formula is A(5), where there are 5 fused stamens and they are epipetalous.

Liliaceae, the lily family, form the representative of the monocot plants. Its as six stamens arranged in sets of three without fusion.

Brassicaceae includes the mustard plant group where the 6 male parts (stamen) of flower are arranges as sets of 2 and 4 without been fused. They are diadelphous.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs consists of false fruits?
questions.solution:
The fertilized mature ovule containing the embryo surrounded by layer of hard coat is generally called as seed. While the ovary in the flowering plant develops into a fruit after fertilization. Fruit is a characteristic feature found in flowering plants. Fruit formed from a group of flowers or inflorescence is called as multiple fruit or composite fruit. Each flower of the inflorescence produces a fruit but all join/fuse into a single mass. Example pineapple and mulberry.

Many a times the bulk of the fruit that is developing is not derived from the ovary but from other floral parts. Such fruits are called as false fruit, pseudo-fruits or accessory fruits.

In apple and pear, the thalamus or floral tube develops around the pericarp producing the bulk of the edible part. Pineapple and mulberry fruits are derived from receptacle of the flower than wholly from the ovary.

In the development of fruit for cashew, the pedicel forms the major bulk of the fruit than ovary.

Atropa belladonna, common name deadly nightshade, is perennial plant. It is a poisonous herb and belong the to the family Solanaceae (tomatoes, potatoes).

The foliage and berries contain tropane alkaloids which are considered extremely toxic on ingestion. These toxins of the plant have been found to cause delirium and hallucinations. Pilocarpine is the antidote for the belladonna.

Plants grown for decorative purpose in gardens, house and landscapes are called as ornamental plants. Roses, daffodils, lilac etc. are considered ornamental plants.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution:
The flower of the angiosperm plant can be categorized depending on the arrangement of the whorls around the gynoecium.

Epigynous flowers have the ovary is in the inferior position as the thalamus surrounds the ovary and may even fuse with it. The other whorls develop over the thalamus. This arrangement is shown by guava, cucumber and ray florets of sunflower.

If the ovary position is above the thalamus, that is superior to other whorls, the arrangement is called hypogynous. Mustard, brinjal develop such flowers.

When the gynoecium and other whorls are arranged almost at same level, the flower is called perigynous and ovary position is considered half inferior. Peach plant has such type of flower arrangement

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Arrange the different parts of the root vertically, from the top to the bottom.
options: Region of elongation → Root hair → Region of maturation → Region of meristematic activity → Root cap
Region of maturation → Root hair → Region of elongation → Region of meristematic activity → Root cap
Region of maturation → Region of elongation → Region of meristematic activity → Root cap → Root hair
Root cap → Region of meristematic activity → Region of elongation → Root hair → Region of maturation
questions.solution:
The root is covered at the apex by a thimble-like structure called the root cap. It protects the tender apex of the root as it makes its way through the soil. A few millimetres above the root cap is the region of meristematic activity. The cells of this region are very small, thin-walled and with dense protoplasm. They divide repeatedly. The cells proximal to this region undergo rapid elongation and enlargement and are responsible for the growth of the root in length. This region is called the region of elongation. The cells of the elongation zone gradually differentiate and mature. Hence, this zone, proximal to region of elongation, is called the region of maturation. From this region some of the epidermal cells form very fine and delicate, thread-like structures called root hairs. These root hairs absorb water and minerals from the soil.

Vertically, from top to bottom, the order is: Region of maturation → Root hair → Region of elongation → Region of meristematic activity → Root cap

The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior, e.g., mustard, china rose and brinjal. In epigynous flowers, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, the other parts of the flower arise above the ovary. Hence, the ovary is said to be inferior as in flowers of guava and cucumber. There may be a variation in the length of filaments within a flower, as in Salvia and mustard. Flowers are termed syncarpous when carpels are fused, as in mustard and tomato. In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part. The ovary is one-chambered but it becomes two-chambered due to the formation of the false septum, e.g., mustard and argemone.

questions.solution:
A flower may be hypogynous, perigynous or epigynous on the basis of position of calyx, corolla and androecium in respect to the ovary. Ovary occupies the highest position in hypogynous flower while other parts are situated below the ovary. In perigynous flowers gynoecium is situated at the centre while other parts are situated on the rim of the thalamus. In epigynous flowers ovary is completely enclosed by thalamus, other floral parts arise above the ovary. Perigynous flowers are found in Plum and Peach.

Hypogynous flowers are found in Hibiscus and Mustard.

questions.solution: The gynoecium is the female reproductive part of flower and its unit is carpel or pistil. If gynoecium carpel may be single (monocarpellary) or several (multicarpellary). In multicarpellary condition, carpels may be free (apocarpous) or fused (syncarpous). Apocarpous gynoecium can be seen in lotus, rose, etc., while syncarpous gynoecium can be seen in mustard, tomato, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A fruit which develops from a polycarpellary, apocarpous gynoecium of a single flower is called
questions.solution: Depending on the arrangement from where they develop, the fruit can be categorized as simple fruits, aggregate fruits, multiple fruits, and accessory fruits. When a fruit develops from a single ovary (monocarpellary) of a single flower it is known as a simple fruit, eg: plum and peaches, which may be fleshy, and walnuts which fall in the dry category. Aggregate fruits are the ones that are formed from several ovaries (polycarpellary) of a single flower, eg: strawberry. Composite or multiple fruits develop from different flowers of a whole inflorescence group together, eg: pineapple, figs etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In guava, cucumber, and ray florets of sunflower, the ovary is
questions.solution: The flowers may be categorized as hypogynous, perigynous, and epigynous depending on the position of calyx, corolla, and androecium with respect to the ovary on the thalamus. When the ovaries are attached above the floral parts or when the gynoecium is at the highest position in a flower, it is known as superior ovary, eg: mustard and brinjal. When the ovary lies below the floral parts and the flower rises above the ovary it is known as inferior ovary, eg: in flowers of guava, cucumber, and ray florets of sunflower. When the gynoecium is in the centre and the floral parts are located on the rim of the thalamus such flowers are known as perigynous flowers and the ovary said to be half inferior or half superior ovary, eg: plum, peach, rose.

options: The reproductive axis shows a large degree of prominent variations.

questions.solution: The floral characters tell us about the flowers and its arrangement, the floral organs and its fusion, on the other hand, the vegetative characters involve the shoot system and the roots. For classification of angiosperms, the floral characters are preferred over the vegetative characters because they are less affected by the external environment and therefore show fewer variations as compared to the vegetative traits of the plant. One more reason for their preference is that the flowers are easy to be carried and greatly vary from each other, which makes the classification easier.

questions.solution: Roots in some plants change their shape and structure and become modified to perform functions other than absorption and conduction of water and minerals. They are modified for support, storage of food and respiration. Tap roots of carrot, turnip and adventitious roots of sweet potato, get swollen and store food. The hanging roots of banyan are called prop roots. Similarly, the stems of maize and sugarcane have supporting roots coming out of the lower nodes of the stem. These are called stilt roots. questions.solution: The male reproductive organ of a flower is known as the stamen. Each stamen has two parts anther and a stalk (filament). When the stamens are found attached to the perianth like in the flowers of Lily they are known as epiphyllous and when they are found attached to the petals like in flowers of brinjal they are known as epipetalous. questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Generally, monocotyledonous seeds are endospermic but some as in orchids are non-endospermic. In the seeds of cereals such as maize the seed coat is membranous and generally fused with the fruit wall. The endosperm is bulky and stores food. The outer covering of endosperm separates the embryo by a proteinous layer called aleurone layer. The embryo is small and situated in a groove at one end of the endosperm. It consists of one large and shield shaped cotyledon known as scutellum and a short axis with a plumule and a radicle. The plumule and radicle are enclosed in sheaths which are called coleoptile and coleorhiza, respectively.
